anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; no supply, driver, or other pin is connected to it.
anomalies.expected: A 3.3 V LED supply or switched 3.3 V driver should be connected to this net so the Ethernet/activity LEDs can conduct through their current-limiting resistors to the open-collector outputs.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 have no anode voltage, so the Pi activity and Ethernet link/activity LEDs will not illuminate.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2) is connected to ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 2 (K2) is connected through R60 back to the same ESTOP_OUT node.
anomalies.expected: The LED should be connected between a voltage source and ESTOP_OUT, for example A2 to a 3.3 V rail and K2 through R60 to ESTOP_OUT, or A2 to ESTOP_OUT and K2 through R60 to GND, so ESTOP_OUT can drive the LED.
anomalies.impact: The second channel of D30 has both ends tied to the same net through a resistor, so it cannot light; the e-stop/CAN status indication is lost.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows two unambiguous LED-drive faults: a floating /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW supply net and D30's second LED tied from ESTOP_OUT back to ESTOP_OUT through R60. These would make the board behave differently from a normally powered LED indication circuit.
